title: Elodie and the Garden Again
premise: Elodie Hartwell, a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter and part-time novelist, has trained her heart like a muscle: contained, rationed, never fully spent. When a snowstorm strands her on Gullwrack Island with Julian Voss — the rival publisher who broke her heart a decade ago and now wants to buy her unfinished manuscript — old wounds and new ambition collide in one small keeper's cottage. As the storm traps them together, Elodie must choose between the safety of lending pieces of herself and the risk of giving the whole heart, while Julian must decide whether winning her story is worth losing her trust. The last ferry of the season forces the choice: she lets him leave with the manuscript but not her forgiveness, then rows out through ice-choked water to stop him at the dock, choosing truth over pride as they finally claim each other.
about_author: O. M. Okafor is the pen name of a former coastal archivist who spent five years cataloguing lighthouse logs before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn romances about stubborn people learning that love is not a resource to be managed.

chapters.title: The Muscle Theory
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. On the mainland ferry, Elodie rehearses her pitch for the Gullwrack Lighthouse Trust while explaining to her sister why hearts are trainable muscles. She's guarded, wry, controlled. Beat: establish her armor and the manuscript she hides from everyone.

chapters.title: Salt and Contracts
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Arriving on Gullwrack, she learns the Trust's new investor is Julian Voss — the rival editor who rejected her novel ten years ago and vanished. Their first meeting crackles with old resentment dressed as professionalism. Beat: dread sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: What the Logs Remember
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian reviews the Trust's finances and realizes the island's survival depends on his firm's approval — leverage he didn't ask for. He tells himself he came for the archive, not for her. Beat: guilt he refuses to name.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Weather
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Inventorying the lighthouse archive, she finds her grandfather's logs and a letter hinting at a family secret about the 1998 wreck. Julian appears; they argue about the past until the radio warns of a historic snowstorm. Beat: the past made physical.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The last ferry is cancelled mid-crossing; both are stranded in the keeper's cottage with failing heat and one generator. Forced proximity strips their professional masks within hours. Beat: claustrophobia becoming unwanted intimacy.

chapters.title: Rationed Light
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Power fails; they share candles and canned soup. Julian admits he left a decade ago because her rejection letter — which she never sent — was found by his mentor. A misunderstanding surfaces. Beat: first crack in the armor.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letter
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian confesses he kept her unsent letter all these years, reading it when his career felt hollow. Elodie is furious that he carried her words without permission. Beat: intimacy weaponized, trust bent.

chapters.title: Storm Work
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They repair the storm shutters together, bodies working in rhythm. Elodie almost kisses him, then retreats behind the muscle theory aloud. Julian calls it cowardice. Beat: desire versus doctrine.

chapters.title: Grandfather's Wreck
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Reading the 1998 log by lamplight, she discovers her grandfather falsified the wreck report to protect a friend — power used kindly, corruption born anyway. She wonders what she'd falsify for love. Beat: theme crystallized.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The night peaks: they sleep together, tender and ruinous. Morning brings silence, because Elodie finds Julian's acquisition memo — the manuscript is an asset line item. Beat: peak warmth curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: Asset
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Confrontation: Julian insists the memo was boilerplate; Elodie hears only valuation. She locks the manuscript away and stops speaking except in logistics. Beat: walls rebuilt higher than before.

chapters.title: Icebound Honesty
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian drafts a resignation letter to his firm rather than let them bury the Trust, but can't send it without signal. He shows Elodie the draft; she reads it as performance. Beat: sincerity misread as strategy.

chapters.title: The Sister's Call
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A satellite phone call from her sister cuts through: their mother is ill, and Elodie's instinct is to handle it alone, contained. Julian watches her ration even grief. Beat: her armor shown hurting someone else.

chapters.title: Borrowed Pieces
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian offers money quietly; Elodie explodes — she doesn't lend pieces, she lends nothing. In the fight, she admits she loves him and hates that she does. Beat: truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Thaw Water
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Storm breaks; ice groans offshore. Elodie rereads her own unsent letter and sees how much of it was fear dressed as discipline. She begins rewriting the manuscript's ending. Beat: turning inward before outward.

chapters.title: The Ferry Schedule
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Radio confirms one emergency ferry tomorrow — the season's last departure. Julian must be on it to deliver his resignation in person or lose everything. Elodie must decide whether to ask him to stay. Neither asks. Beat: the ticking clock set.

chapters.title: Last Night, First Draft
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She gives Julian the manuscript to read overnight — the whole heart, unguarded. He reads till dawn and weeps at the ending she changed. Beat: vulnerability offered without terms.

chapters.title: Departure
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. At the dock, Julian boards with the manuscript and leaves his resignation undelivered, choosing to return to her instead — but Elodie, expecting abandonment, has already walked away. Beat: tragic near-miss, climax ignition.

chapters.title: Through the Ice
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Learning he stayed, Elodie rows across freezing harbor water to reach the dock before the ferry departs, nearly capsizing. Her grandfather's logs taught her: some risks you take whole. Beat: physical climax mirroring emotional surrender.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the dock, soaked and shaking, Elodie declares herself — no pieces, no contracts, no conditions. Julian tears up the acquisition memo and proposes partnership, personal and professional. Beat: mutual surrender, loyalty chosen over advantage.

chapters.title: Relit
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Weeks later: the Trust saved, the wreck secret published with the family's blessing, mother recovering. Elodie mails the finished manuscript under her real name. Beat: belonging earned, truth honored.

chapters.title: Garden Again
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POV. Spring on Gullwrack: they plant the ruined garden behind the lighthouse together. Elodie's new book opens with a line about a heart that isn't a muscle after all. Beat: quiet, earned resolution — growth after storm.
